text:
maria: deploybot flagged canary latency p95 up ~320ms vs baseline ~180ms. Not enough errors to trigger auto-rollback but it's noisy. link to telemetry: https://telemetry.internal/runs/4200

deploy-bot: [AUTOMATION] Canary check: region=us-west-2 model=v2.5.0 traffic=10% p95=320ms (+78%) thresholds: rollback=+100% -> no auto-rollback. Recent deploys: kernel-opt-2, kv-cache-flags. logs: https://logs.internal/canary/4200

raj: hmm, 78% is concerning but could be warmup. Is this concentrated on a single host or across the pool?

sam: I see the spike on pool-a node-7, traces show KV cache misses during prefix load. Cold-start heavy. Might be the new kernel ordering.

maria: options: 1) manual rollback to v2.4.8 (safe), 2) increase canary to 30% to surface signal faster (risky), 3) patch KV flags and re-run canary (no fast turnaround). Thoughts?

ops-oncall: don't widen canary mid-investigation. If customer-facing p95 is degraded we should roll back to maintain SLOs. Also notify CS + docs for comms. @cs-team

maria: ok calling for manual rollback if we don't have a mitigation in 10m. drafting internal and customer notes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: To execute manual rollback run:
```
deploybot rollback --to v2.4.8 --scope=100% --reason "canary p95 delta 78%" --notify=ops,cs,docs
```

raj: +1 to rollback. I'll capture artifacts and tag the changelist for the follow-up.

sam: I'll keep collecting traces and heap profiles, uploading to the traceboard: https://intra/trace/4200

docs-team: I'll stand by to update release notes and incident blurb after rollback completes.

maria: executing rollback now. tagging @ops-oncall for validation.

deploy-bot: ACTION: rollback started by maria at 4200000020. Steps: draining canary, switching traffic, verifying healthchecks. ETA ~5m.

ops-oncall: observing p95 returning to ~190ms within 2m of traffic shift. continuing 15m monitoring window.

deploy-bot: ACTION: rollback completed at 4200000045. traffic at v2.4.8 =100%. healthchecks OK.

maria: thanks all. I'll publish the customer note draft to #release-notes and create a short postmortem to capture kernel/kv interactions. :thumbsup:
